method: Disk-grounded cross-check only (no live IDA session run in this pass): (1) read 1.0.9 relay-core manifest.json cluster list (19 clusters) as the target universe; (2) read 1.2.3 relay manifest.json declared scope (core::relay::* 32 submodules + commands::relay 23 commands); (3) diff the 32 raw/aimami/1.2.3/macos-arm64/core/relay/ submodule directory names and a sample of function filenames against the 19 relay-core-1.0.9 cluster names/functions; (4) cross-read REVERSE-STATUS.md (canonical claim/status ledger) for any existing project determination on this exact question.
verdict: PARTIAL — not a clean covered_by_relay_bundle=true. Authoritative project ledger (REVERSE-STATUS.md, <审计会话> entry, dated 2026-07-24) already and independently lists `relay-core` as a distinct, still-open 1.2.3 full-app backlog target (macOS + Windows + a cross-platform relay-core-bootstrap module), explicitly separate from the already-closed `relay` bundle. Function-name-level content overlap is substantial for most 1.0.9 relay-core clusters, but two clusters have no discoverable 1.2.3 equivalent, and formal RULE-9 diff/migration + reduce into a canonical audits/<platform>-1.2.3-relay-core/ bundle has never been run.
covered_by_relay_bundle_caveat: Most 1.0.9 relay-core cluster content is present, function-name-verified, inside audits/macos-1.2.3-relay/'s declared core::relay::* 32-submodule scope (content-level absorption). But (a) this absorption was never formally verified via RULE-9 diff/migration -- macos-1.2.3-relay/manifest.json's consumed_bundles list does not include audits/macos-1.0.9-relay-core/, so the 1.2.3 relay baseline was produced as a fresh independent baseline, not as a diff against relay-core-1.0.9; (b) 2 of 19 clusters (relay_web_executor, relay_web_tools) have zero name/function matches anywhere in the 1.2.3 macos-arm64 raw tree; (c) REVERSE-STATUS.md's own 2026-07-24 full-app gap audit already lists relay-core as open/unreduced, including Windows-side raw evidence that exists but has not been reduced to canonical form.
